questions.question: When were the general elections to the Legislative Assembly of the National Capital Region held for the first time?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**In 1993**__.

__
 
• The** First Legislative Assembly of Delhi** was established in** November 1993**, following the replacement of the** Council of Ministers **with the **Delhi Legislative Assembly **through the **Constitution Act of 1991** and the **Government of National Capital Territory of Delhi Act, 1991,** which was facilitated by the Sixty-ninth Amendment to the Indian Constitution.
 
• This amendment officially designated the Union Territory of Delhi as the National Capital Territory of Delhi, subsequently enabling Delhi to conduct its first state elections.
 
• During these elections, a total of six national parties, three state parties, forty-one registered (unrecognized) parties, and various independent candidates vied for the 70 assembly seats.
 
• The Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP) secured a majority with 49 seats and subsequently formed the government. 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The** inaugural General Elections of India **commenced on October 25th, 1951, and concluded on February 21st, 1952.
 
• The Indian National Congress emerged victorious in a landslide, and Jawaharlal Nehru assumed office as India's first democratically elected Prime Minister.

questions.question: Which of the following articles of the Constitution of India states that no religious instruction shall be imparted in any educational institution wholly maintained out of State funds?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Article 28**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Article 28** addresses the **issue of religious freedom** concerning attendance at **religious instruction or worship **within certain educational institutions.
 
• It stipulates:
 
 
• **Religious instruction** is prohibited in educational institutions that are entirely funded by the State.
 
• However, this prohibition does not extend to educational institutions administered by the State but established under a trust mandating religious instruction.
 
• Nevertheless, individuals attending such institutions cannot be forced to participate in religious instruction or attend religious worship.
 
• For minors, attending such activities requires the consent of their guardian.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Article 40 **of the Indian Constitution outlines one of the Directive Principles of State Policy, which mandates that the State must take measures to organize village panchayats.
 
• **Article 68 **of the Constitution of India specifies that an election to fill a vacancy in the office of Vice-President must be concluded before the end of the term.
 
• **Article 54 **of the Constitution of India pertains to the election process for the President of India.

questions.question: How is the molecular weight of a fatty acid determined?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Saponification value**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **The saponification value** denotes the quantity of milligrams of **potassium hydroxide (KOH) or sodium hydroxide (NaOH)** needed to saponify one gram of fat, given specific conditions.
 
• This value serves as a gauge of the average molecular weight, or chain length, of the fatty acids contained within the sample in the form of triglycerides.
 
• In essence, a higher saponification value indicates a lower average length of fatty acids and a lighter mean molecular weight of triglycerides, while a lower value suggests the opposite.
 
• In practical terms, fats or oils possessing a high saponification value, such as coconut and palm oil, are more favorable for soap making.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **The peroxide value (PV)** of an edible oil quantifies the degree of primary oxidation of unsaturated fats within the oil, primarily through the conversion of molecular oxygen into hydroperoxides and peroxides.
 
• **The acid value (AV)** is a numerical representation of the acidity level of a chemical substance, typically expressed in terms of the quantity of potassium hydroxide (KOH) required to neutralize the free acids present in one gram of the substance.
 
• **The iodine value (IV)** measures the mass of iodine in grams consumed by 100 grams of a chemical substance. It serves as an indicator of the degree of unsaturation or the number of double bonds present in the fatty acids comprising the substance, with higher values indicating greater unsaturation.

questions.question: Buland Darwaza located in Fatehpur Sikri is the entrance gate of which of the following mosques?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Jama Masjid**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **The Buland Darwaza **serves as the primary entrance to the **Jama Masjid located in Fatehpur Sikri**.
 
• It known as** "Door of Victory," **it was constructed by the **Mughal emperor Akbar in 1575** to commemorate his triumph over Gujarat.
 
• Renowned for its Mughal architecture, the Buland Darwaza stands as the world's tallest gateway, soaring at a height of 53.63 meters and spanning 35 meters in width, accessible via 42 steps.
 
• The Jama Masjid, a magnificent mosque, was completed in 1571.
 
• It features a central nave, along with two colonnaded halls and two square chambers crowned by domes.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **The Jama Masjid **is a 16th-century congregational mosque situated within the UNESCO World Heritage Site of Fatehpur Sikri, located in Uttar Pradesh, India.
 
• Constructed by the Mughal emperor Akbar, it held the distinction of being the largest mosque within the empire during its construction period.
 
• Drawing inspiration from earlier mosques built by various pre-Mughal sultanates, the Jama Masjid served as a significant influence on subsequent Mughal architectural styles.
 
• Within the mosque complex, notable monuments include the Buland Darwaza, which functions as the southern gateway to the mosque, and the Tomb of Salim Chishti.
 
• This tomb is dedicated to the revered saint Salim Chishti, in whose honor the mosque was originally erected.

questions.question: In which sport Mariyappan Thangavelu and Sharad Kumar won silver and bronze medals at Tokyo Paralympics?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**High jump**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• India's remarkable performance at the **Tokyo Paralympics **persisted as** Mariyappan Thangavelu and Sharad Kumar** clinched silver and bronze respectively in the men's high jump T63 event.
 
• **Sharad cleared 1.83m,** while Mariyappan achieved his best clearance at 1.86m.
 
• U.S. athlete Sam Grewe, the reigning world champion, secured gold by clearing 1.88m on his third attempt.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• With this achievement,** India's medal tally** at the **Paralympics now stands at 10**, comprising **two golds, five silvers, and three bronzes.**
 
• Notably, Mariyappan had previously secured gold in this event at the Rio Paralympics, with Varun Singh Bhati earning bronze and Sharad finishing sixth. In the Tokyo event, Bhati secured 7th place after clearing 1.77m.
 
• This event mirrored the success of the 2016 Paralympics, with India claiming two of the three podium spots.
 
• Mariyappan now joins Joginder Singh Bedi and Devendra Jhajharia as one of the few Indians to win multiple medals at the Paralympics, with Jhajharia and Bedi each having secured three medals.

questions.question: Which of the following classical dances begins with a drumming performance called "Kelikottu"?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Kathakali**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Kathakali **begins with a **drumming performance** called **"Kelikottu"**.
 
• Kelikottu serves as a brief drumming passage heralding the commencement of the performance, typically held within **temple premises after nightfall**.
 
• Following Kelikottu is the **Todayam**, during which one or two characters seek the blessings of the gods.
 
• Subsequently, the Purappadu ensues, featuring a pure Nritya (dance) piece.
 
• During Kelikottu, the harmonious interplay of drums and cymbals accompanies the proceedings, enhancing the auditory experience.
 
• The drums employed in Kelikottu encompass a variety, including the resonant Kettledrum, the classic timpani, and the elongated Maddalam drum.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Kathakali,** a classical Indian dance form, finds its roots in Kerala, a southern state of India.
 
• **Odissi, **a classical Indian dance form, traces its origins to the sacred precincts of Odisha, an eastern coastal state of India.
 
• **Kuchipudi, **a captivating dance-drama, originated in the village of Kuchipudi, nestled in Andhra Pradesh, India.
 
• **Bharatanatyam, **another classical Indian dance form, has its origins in Tamil Nadu.

questions.question: Dance couple Kamalini and Nalini Asthana have been awarded the Padma Shri in 2022. He is famous for which of the following dance styles?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Kathak**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Kamalini Asthana and Nalini Asthana**, hailing from **Agra, Uttar Pradesh,** form a celebrated sister duo renowned for their exceptional performances in the **Benaras Gharana style of Kathak.**
 
• Their dedication to promoting this style both within India and internationally has earned them widespread acclaim.
 
• Their inaugural overseas journey occurred in 1983 when they participated in the **UFTAA Conference in Paris, France.**
 
• Initially planned for a mere two weeks, their tour extended unexpectedly for nearly two and a half years.
 
• Throughout this extensive excursion, they mesmerized audiences with their Kathak performances in various international locales, including Torremolinos and Madrid in Spain, Dublin in Ireland, and the ISKCON in London.
 
• Kamalini and Nalini achieved a remarkable feat by showcasing their talent at the staggering altitude of 18,000 feet at Kailash Mansarovar and Badri Nath.
 
• Their remarkable contributions to the realm of art were duly recognized by the Government of India in 2022 when they were honored with the prestigious Padma Shri award, a testament to their distinguished service in the field of Kathak.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Kathak, o**ne of the eight principal forms of Indian classical dance, traces its origins to the itinerant bards of ancient northern India, known as** Kathakars or storytellers**.
 
• The term "Kathak" is derived from the Sanskrit word **"Katha," meaning "story," and "Kathakar,"** which translates to "the one who tells a story" or "related to stories."
 
• Kathak is synonymous with the art of storytelling, encompassing intricate footwork, graceful movements, and emotive expressions.
 
• Primarily prevalent in northern India, Kathak holds historical significance akin to Bharatanatyam in the south and Odissi in the east, alongside other prominent classical dance forms across South Asia.

questions.question: In which of the following sports the clean and jerk technique is used?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Weight Lifting**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Modern Olympic** weightlifting **consists of two main stages: **the snatch and the clean and jerk.**
 
• During the snatch, the weightlifter swiftly raises the barbell above their head in a single fluid motion.
 
• In the clean and jerk, the weightlifter first hoists the barbell to their chest (clean), then, after pausing, extends their arms and legs to elevate it above their head (jerk) with straight elbows, maintaining this position until a buzzer signals completion.
 
• Each weightlifter receives three attempts for both the snatch and the clean and jerk.
 
• The highest successful lift in each stage is recorded, and the combined weight lifted determines the overall winner.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

• **Wrestling**, a martial art and combat sport, revolves around grappling with an opponent, aiming to secure a positional advantage via various throws or techniques, adhering to specific rules.
 
• **The hammer throw,** among the four throwing events in standard outdoor track and field competitions, alongside the discus throw, shot put, and javelin, requires athletes to hurl a heavy hammer for distance.

questions.question: Which style of architecture was used in Lakshmi Vilas Palace in Vadodara, Gujarat?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Indo-arabic**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Indo-Arabic architecture** was used in **Lakshmi Vilas Palace in Vadodara**, Gujarat.
 
• Constructed in **1890 by Maharaja Sayajirao Gaekwad III,** the Lakshmi Vilas Palace in Vadodara, Gujarat, showcases the Indo-Saracenic architectural style.
 
• This fusion style harmonizes Indian, Islamic, and European architectural elements, such as Mughal, Gothic, and Hindu influences.
 
• Spanning 500 acres, the palace boasts exquisite Belgian stained glass and authentic teak woodwork.
 
• Its interior evokes the grandeur of a sprawling European country estate, complete with modern amenities like elevators.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Indo-Islamic architecture** embodies the architectural style of the Indian subcontinent, crafted by and for Islamic patrons and purposes. 
 
• Its roots trace back to the establishment of Delhi as the capital of the Ghurid dynasty in 1193, marking the inception of significant developments in this architectural tradition. 
 
• The subsequent Delhi Sultanate, comprising various Central Asian dynasties, and later the Mughal Empire from the 15th century onward, further advanced Indo-Islamic architecture. 
 
• These dynasties facilitated the integration of Islamic architectural and artistic styles from West Asia into the fabric of the Indian subcontinent.

questions.question: What was the theme of Independence Day in India in the year 2015?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Towards True Freedom**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Towards True Freedom **was the theme of Independence Day in India in the year **2015**.
 
• The theme **"Towards True Freedom"** for Independence Day in India in 2015 likely aimed to reflect on the progress made since India's independence in 1947 and to emphasize the ongoing journey towards achieving true freedom and prosperity for all citizens.
 
• It might have focused on various aspects such as socio-economic development, political empowerment, cultural diversity, and individual liberties.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Independence Day** is celebrated annually on August 15th in India as a public holiday, commemorating the nation's freedom from British rule on August 15, 1947.
 
• This marks the enactment of the Indian Independence Act, transferring legislative sovereignty to the Indian Constituent Assembly.
 
• Although King George VI remained the head of state until the transition to a republic, India formally adopted the Constitution on January 26, 1950, becoming the Republic of India and replacing the prefix "Dominion of India."
 
• India's path to independence was characterized by a notable independence movement, known for its largely non-violent resistance and civil disobedience, led by the Indian National Congress under the guidance of Mahatma Gandhi.
 
• Gandhi drew inspiration from earlier Indian movements, including one led by Ram Singh Kuka, advocating for principles such as non-violence, self-reliance, and civil disobedience throughout the struggle for independence.

questions.question: What does "Green Revolution" mean in Indian agriculture?

options.text: Extraordinary increase in food grain production

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Extraordinary increase in food grain production**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **The Green Revolution **signifies a significant advancement in agricultural practices aimed at enhancing production through the integration of modern tools and techniques.
 
• It marks a pivotal period in which agricultural systems transitioned into industrialized models, owing to the adoption of innovative methods such as the **utilization of high-yielding variety seeds, tractors, irrigation systems, pesticides, and fertilizers.**
 
• Prior to 1967, governmental efforts primarily focused on expanding agricultural land to meet growing food demands. However, the exponential rise in population outpaced food production, necessitating urgent measures to boost yields.
 
• This urgency culminated in the implementation of the Green Revolution, which revolutionized agricultural productivity and played a crucial role in addressing food scarcity challenges.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Prime Minister Narendra Modi** has given approval for the implementation of the **Umbrella Scheme Green Revolution – 'Krishonnati Yojana' **in the agriculture sector, covering a three-year period from 2017 to 2020.
 
• This initiative includes 11 schemes aimed at fostering holistic and scientific development in the agriculture and allied sectors.
 
• The central share allocated for this scheme amounts to Rs. 33,269.976 crore. The overarching objective of the Green Revolution - Krishonnati Yojana is to enhance farmer income by boosting productivity, production, and improving returns on agricultural produce.
 
• It seeks to fortify production infrastructure, lower production costs, and facilitate the marketing of agricultural and allied products.

questions.question: Who is given the credit for starting the Gupta period?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Chandra Gupta I**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Chandragupta I **is widely acknowledged as the progenitor of the **Gupta dynasty,** which commenced around **319–320 CE.**
 
• Originally a local chief within the** realm of Magadha,** encompassing portions of modern Bihar state, Chandra Gupta I gradually augmented his authority, domain, riches, and renown.
 
• By forging strategic matrimonial alliances, he elevated himself to the **status of Maharajadhiraja,** signifying **"Emperor" or "King of Kings",** in the year 320 CE.
 
• Through military conquests, he expanded his dominion significantly, stretching from the Ganges River to Prayaga by 321 AD.
 
• Chandragupta I instituted coinage bearing the joint names of himself and his queen, solidifying their shared authority.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Samudragupta, **the second emperor of the Gupta Empire, is esteemed as one of India's most illustrious rulers. Born to Emperor Chandragupta I and Princess Kumaradevi of the Licchavi dynasty, Samudragupta significantly bolstered his dynasty's political and military authority.
 
• **Chandragupta II,** also recognized by the title Vikramaditya, succeeded his father Samudragupta as the third ruler of the Gupta Empire. Continuing his father's policy of territorial expansion, Chandragupta II pursued military conquests to further augment the empire's domain.
 
• **Kumaragupta I,** an emperor of the Gupta Empire, was the son of Emperor Chandragupta II and Queen Dhruvadevi. He appears to have effectively governed the inherited territory, which spanned from Gujarat in the west to the Bengal region in the east.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Anamudi Peak,** towering at **8,842 ft (2,695 m) above sea level,** claims the title of the **highest peak in South India.**
 
• Nestled within the **Ernakulam and Idukki districts of Kerala,** within the Western Ghats mountain range, Anamudi is often hailed as the "Himalayas of South India".
 
• It beckons adventurers with its allure for hiking and trekking, offering panoramic vistas of the surrounding valleys, cascading waterfalls, and lush forests.
 
• This majestic peak serves as a habitat for a diverse array of wildlife, including Asian elephants, endangered gaurs, nilgiri langurs, and lion-tailed macaques.
 
• The moniker "Anamudi" derives from the Malayalam language, meaning "elephant's forehead", a tribute to its distinctive resemblance to the head of an elephant.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Doddabetta**, towering at 2,637 meters, claims the title of the highest mountain in the Nilgiri Mountains. It is surrounded by a reserved forest area that adds to its natural allure.
 
• **Mukurthi Peak**, standing tall at 2,554 meters, is nestled within the Nilgiri mountains of Tamil Nadu, India. This peak ranks among the highest summits in the Western Ghats and holds the distinction of being the fourth highest peak in the Nilgiri Hills.
 
• **Mahendragiri**, situated in the Rayagada block of the Gajapati district in Odisha, India, rises to a height of 1,501 meters (4,925 ft). It secures the position of the second highest mountain peak in Odisha, adding to the scenic beauty of the region.

questions.question: In which of the following years, the Nawab of Awadh accepted the subsidiary alliance initiated by Lord Wellesley, the Governor General of British India?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**1801**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **In 1801, the Nawab of Awadh, Saadat Ali Khan II,** entered into the **Subsidiary Alliance** with the British.
 
• This alliance was devised as a political and military strategy by** Lord Wellesley, **the **Governor-General of British India, in 1798**.
 
• The terms of the Subsidiary Alliance included several stipulations:
 
 
• The Nawab was required to cede nearly half of his kingdom to the British, encompassing territories such as Rohilkhand and the region between the Ganga and the Jamuna rivers.
 
• The Nawab had to disband his own troops and rely instead on a British-managed army.
 
• The Nawab was obligated to pay substantial subsidies, often amounting to several lakhs of rupees.
 
• Article IV of the treaty affirmed that the forces provided by the British East India Company were deemed adequate to safeguard the ruler of Awadh.
 
• These terms effectively diminished the autonomy of the Nawab and established British dominance in Awadh.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Richard Colley Wellesley,** 1st Marquess Wellesley, was an Anglo-Irish politician and colonial administrator.
 
• He initially held the title of Viscount Wellesley until 1781 when he inherited his father's title as the 2nd Earl of Mornington.
 
• Later, in 1799, he was bestowed with the Irish peerage title of Marquess Wellesley. Additionally, he held the title of Lord Wellesley in the Peerage of Great Britain.

questions.question: In 1921–22 the farmers of the Malabar coast of Kerala organized a great revolt, known as ______.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Moplah rebellion**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• In 1921–22 the** farmers of the Malabar coast of Kerala** organized a great revolt, known as **Moplah rebellion**.
 
• **The Moplah Rebellion,** also termed the Moplah Riots of 1921, marked a series of uprisings by Mappila Muslims in Kerala during the 19th and early 20th centuries, primarily directed against the **British rule and Hindu landlords** in Malabar (Northern Kerala).
 
• This armed revolt was spearheaded by** Variyamkunnath Kunjahammed Haji.**
 
• The interpretation of the Moplah uprising remains contentious, with some viewing it as a nationalist resistance against British authority, while others characterize it as a series of communal clashes.
 
• Sir C. Shankaran Nair, a former President of the Indian National Congress, criticized Gandhi's endorsement of the Khilafat Movement as a contributing factor to the violence witnessed during the rebellion.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **The Kol rebellion, **alternately referred to as the Kol uprising or the Kol mutiny, unfolded as an insurrection by the Kol people of Chhota Nagpur, India, spanning from 1831 to 1832.
 
• **The Munda Rebellion**, also recognized as the Munda Ulgulan, emerged as a tribal uprising in the latter part of the 19th century.
 
• **The Santhal Rebellion,** also termed the Sonthal Rebellion or the Santhal Hool, transpired as a peasant revolt during the years 1855 to 1856.

questions.question: Which of the following musical instruments is played by Nandini and Ragini Shankar?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Violin**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **The violin **is played by **Nandini and Ragini Shankar.**
 
• **Ragini and Nandini Shankar,** violinists based in Mumbai, have gained recognition for their remarkable skill in interpreting vocal music on the violin.
 
• The duo has collaborated with renowned artists across diverse genres and recently joined forces with **Decca Records US **to form their fusion ensemble, **Taraana**.
 
• **Ragini Shankar **has been honoured with the prestigious** Aditya Birla Kala Kiran Award** and the esteemed **Jashn-e-Youngistan Award**, bestowed upon her by the Vice President of India.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **The violin,** colloquially referred to as a fiddle, is a** wooden chordophone**, serving as the **smallest and highest-pitched instrument** (soprano) within the violin family.
 
• It holds significant importance across a diverse array of musical genres.
 
• Notably, violins feature prominently in Western classical music, whether as part of ensembles ranging from chamber groups to orchestras or as solo instruments.
 
• Additionally, they play a crucial role in various folk music traditions, including country, bluegrass, and jazz.
 
• Originating in 16th-century Italy, the violin underwent further modifications during the 18th and 19th centuries to enhance its sound quality and projection capabilities.

questions.question: Who is the author of the novel 'A Suitable Boy' which is one of the longest novels?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Vikram Seth**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **"A Suitable Boy," **penned by **Vikram Seth** and released in 1993, stands as one of the** lengthiest novels published in a single volume**, boasting **1,349 pages** (1,488 pages in paperback) in its English edition.
 
• This narrative unfolds against the backdrop of post-independence, post-partition India, intricately woven across 19 parts, each delving into a distinct subplot.
 
• Vikram Seth, an acclaimed Indian novelist and poet, has authored numerous novels and poetry collections.
 
• His literary prowess has garnered him prestigious accolades, including** the Padma Shri, Sahitya Academy Award, Pravasi Bharatiya Samman, WH Smith Literary Award, and Crossword Book Award.**
 
• Seth's contributions to Indian English language poetry, particularly through works like "Mappings" and "Beastly Tales," have left a lasting imprint on the literary landscape.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Rohinton Mistry, **an Indian-born Canadian author, has garnered numerous accolades throughout his career, including the prestigious Neustadt International Prize for Literature in 2012.
 
• **R.K. Narayan,** hailed as one of the preeminent Indian authors of the twentieth century, was born in 1906. His contributions to literature earned him the National Prize of the Indian Literary Academy, India's foremost literary distinction.
 
• **Salman Rushdie**, an Indian-born British-American novelist, is renowned for his unique blend of magic realism and historical fiction. His works often explore the interplay between Eastern and Western civilizations, with a particular focus on the Indian subcontinent, addressing themes of connection, disruption, and migration.

questions.question: Which of the following indicators presents the picture of occupational structure and unemployment in India?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Labor force participation**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Labour force participation** presents the picture of occupational structure and unemployment in India.
 
• The **Labour Force Participation Rate (LFPR)** in India, as per data from the** Centre for Monitoring Indian Economy (CMIE)**, has dwindled to a mere 40%, dropping from an already meager** 47% in 2016**.
 
• This indicates that more than half of India's working-age population (15 years and above) is opting out of the workforce, and this trend seems to be escalating.
 
• LFPR essentially signifies the percentage of the working-age population seeking employment.
 
• The primary cause for India's low LFPR is the remarkably low participation of women in the workforce.
 
• As of December 2021, while the **male LFPR stood at 67.4%**, the **female LFPR **was alarmingly **low at 9.4%**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The **low LFPR** among women in India can be attributed **to various factors** related to working conditions, including inadequate law enforcement, inefficient public transportation, prevalence of violence against women, and societal norms that discourage women from seeking employment.
 
• These factors create an environment that is not conducive for women to enter the workforce.
 
• Furthermore, while the unemployment rate measures those actively seeking employment but unable to find it, it fails to account for individuals who have become discouraged and stopped looking for work altogether.
 
• This phenomenon often occurs when individuals of working age become disheartened by prolonged unemployment and lose hope in finding suitable employment opportunities.
